finding: A normal catalog Play selected live HLS through the existing vod_index_pending fallback. An actual Lua OSC timeline hit replaced its session; captured normal HTTP 200 responses accepted sequence 1 on the changed session/generation with the same client. Advancing DV state and successful mapper callbacks were subsequently observed. This qualifies one runtime boundary of the previously merged Player repair, not a new production fix or a reproduction of spontaneous DV loss.

method.launch: Agent activated Play in a task-created ordinary Chrome catalog window after confirmed unlock. Existing authentication, normal installed Player options and capabilities.
method.route: Fresh server stdout contains three typed vod_index_pending recoveries for the selected source/window. Correct authoritative Hiqlite route rows and actual live film metadata independently confirm live presentation. The earlier catalog/index census is not represented as an immediately-before-play measurement.
method.route_changes: No quality choice, settings change, forced capability, index removal or synthetic handoff.
method.main_gesture: Agent sent ordinary mpv mouse movement, waited 0.3 s, then button0 single at the actual Cinema timeline. This executes the Lua hit test and normal Python outside-range handler, rather than directly injecting osc-film-seek.
method.control_observation: Passive loopback capture of normal Player request/response traffic; no observer-generated HTTP control POSTs.
method.scope: Software IPC, authoritative route state, sanitized HTTP fields and the project mapper ABI. No optical or attended visual acceptance.

osc_replacement.renderer_target_generation_note: Physical target generation1 is separate from control generation UUIDs and control epoch1. A new control session need not change the physical target generation.

captured_control_exchanges.sequence7_time_origin_note: BindingB sequence7 packet UTC15:35:24.619010 precedes the helper endpoint15:35:25.071887, but its capture-processing event was emitted about 0.530 s after that endpoint. The completed trace containsB1–7; the helper summary had observed only B2–6 as later accepts at its cutoff.
captured_control_exchanges.no409_limit: No409 in the captured known normal-control exchanges. This is scoped to this capture, not a guarantee for future sessions.

post_replacement_DV_observation.scope: The 30.0579-second control observation is not 30 seconds of continuous DV progression or mapping. Only the later 7.594-second sampled span shows the reported 7.466-second DV clock advance.

mapper_probe.clock_alignment: The raw probe origin numerically aligns with recorded CLOCK_BOOTTIME. It is not assumed equal to Python CLOCK_MONOTONIC; full-second buckets start at BPF BEGIN.
mapper_probe.limits: PID-scoped project ABI aggregate callbacks, not paired individual frames or proof of displayed output. Phase labels follow time alignment; callback records carry no session identifier. Resets surround deliberate startup/replacement/cleanup. Configured180seconds and post-exit walltime are not playback coverage.

capture_quality.retained_fields: Only protocol, sequence, accepted_sequence, control generation/epoch, hashed session/client identity, HTTP status and clocks. Public receipt replaces correlation identities with A/B/C.
capture_quality.counter_interpretation: Tool-reported receive/captured counters are not used as a packet-loss ratio. Tcpdump reports zero packets dropped by kernel.
capture_quality.parser_limits: First HTTPexchange per connection (normal installed urllib requests close connections); bounded reassembly. No chunked/close-delimited bodies, IP fragments or IPv6 extension headers. Not PID-attributed; request identities correlate with authoritative session rows.
capture_quality.clock_note: PacketUTC is PCAP capture time; observed monotonic/boottime are later processing clocks and can lag packet delivery.

observer.interpretation: Ended when the agent quit the task-owned Player. IPCclosure/exit1 is not a test pass or an unexplained playback failure.

cleanup.watch_restoration_scope: Normal UI semantic reset to zero/unwatched, not byte-identical restoration of the initially absent watch row. A new zero-position row exists. No direct database write was used.

sequence_repair.qualification: Earlier 105 affected tests/main-lane receipts are inherited; no Player source tests were rerun. This new result adds one bounded actual replacement observation.

provenance.fallback_hash_input_definition: Exact UTF-8 bytes of retained server-fallback-private.json: collector JSON stdout containing selected, ANSI-stripped deployed log lines. Not the entire unfiltered server log.

limits: One ordinary live-source replacement, not every title, route, future replacement or full-film acceptance.
The original spontaneous 6–24-second persistent DV-loss claim remains unreproduced; this trial adds acceptance for the separate already-merged control-sequence repair.
A successful control receipt is independent of video-frame readiness. The observed 30-second control window must not be described as 30 seconds continuously mapped DV.
Target-active/decoder properties and mapped ABI returns do not prove every decoded or displayed frame, optical accuracy or full Dolby Vision fidelity.
The primary helper failed its cleanup criterion; follow-up normal UI reset changed watch state semantically and did not restore an absent row.
No production patch, package change, forced capability, manual index invalidation or display-setting change was introduced; no new production fix is claimed.
This measurement grants no new Player unit-test qualification; repository integrity validation is recorded separately.

latency_observation.clock_limits: BPF bin bounds use its measured alignment with recorded boottime; packet UTC differences compare capture realtime with runner realtime. Capture-processing/helper-observation differences use their separately recorded monotonic times. No subsecond recovery latency is inferred from full-second callback buckets.
latency_observation.interpretation: Control acceptance precedes resumed mapped playback. About 27 seconds of recovery is characterized here, not fixed or accepted as low-latency UX; its cause is not established.
latency_observation.diagnostic_narrowing: About 25.55 seconds separates the replacement curl Opening diagnostic from the first MIME-type diagnostic, before the visible demux and decoder setup. This narrows the observed delay to stream opening/startup, but does not isolate its underlying cause.
latency_observation.diagnostic_timestamp_limit: These are observer receipt timestamps and retained log ordering; buffering may affect timing. They are not wire time-to-first-byte or proof that server bytes were unavailable. The interval is not demonstrated to be spent in client probing, decoding or mapping.
